title: Find the Number of Ways to Place People II
summary: Given a 2D array of points, where each point is represented by a pair of coordinates, determine the number of valid pairs of points where one point is designated as Alice's position and the other as Bob's position.
statement: Given a 2D array of points, where each point is represented by a pair of coordinates, determine the number of valid pairs of points where one point is designated as Alice's position and the other as Bob's position. Alice must be at the upper left corner of the rectangular fence, and Bob must be at the lower right corner. The condition is that no other point should lie within or on the boundary of the fence.
constraints: points contains up to 1,000 distinct signed coordinates.
Alice at A must satisfy A.x≤B.x and A.y≥B.y; boundary points also block the fence.
Count valid role pairs in O(n²) time.
hints: Sorted x order reduces rectangle emptiness to visibility among later y coordinates.
Sort equal x by descending y, then count bounded record-high later y values for every Alice.
For each sorted point, scan right; when max_seen_y<y≤alice_y count the pair and raise max_seen_y.
A non-record candidate has a prior point on or inside its fence, while every bounded record candidate has no such blocker.
editorial: A non-record candidate has a prior point on or inside its fence, while every bounded record candidate has no such blocker.

tests.explanation: No point is upper-left of a point to its right, so the answer is zero.
Only the two consecutive descending pairs avoid enclosing the third point.
